tagline: Pick colors with contrast checker and palette generator
pageDescription: Use this color picker online free to select any color and instantly convert between HEX, RGB, HSL, CMYK and LAB formats. Built-in WCAG contrast checker ensures your color combinations meet accessibility standards, while the palette generator creates harmonious schemes with complementary, analogous and triadic options. Simulate color blindness (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia) to verify your design works for all users. Use the eyedropper tool to sample colors from any element on screen. Generate smooth CSS gradients, export values as Tailwind CSS classes or raw CSS variables, and build complete design tokens — all browser-based with no signup required.

instructions.title: How to use Color Picker

steps.title: Select a color
steps.description: Click on the color wheel or spectrum to pick a color visually, use the eyedropper to sample a color from your screen, or type a value directly in HEX, RGB, or HSL format.

steps.title: Convert between formats
steps.description: Once a color is selected, view its value in all supported formats — HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV, CMYK, and LAB. Click any value to copy it to your clipboard instantly.

steps.title: Check contrast and accessibility
steps.description: Use the WCAG contrast checker to test your foreground and background color combination. The tool shows contrast ratio and pass/fail status for AA and AAA compliance levels.

steps.title: Generate a palette
steps.description: Create color palettes using harmonious schemes: complementary, analogous, triadic, split-complementary, or monochromatic. Adjust saturation and lightness to fine-tune each swatch.

steps.title: Export your colors
steps.description: Copy individual color values, export your palette as CSS custom properties, Tailwind CSS config, or download the full palette for use in your design system or codebase.

troubleshooting: Eyedropper not working: The EyeDropper API requires Chrome 95+ or Edge 95+. It is not supported in Firefox or Safari yet.
Color looks different on screen vs print: Screen uses RGB (additive), print uses CMYK (subtractive). Use the CMYK output for print-accurate values.
Contrast ratio too low: Try increasing the lightness difference between foreground and background. Dark text on light backgrounds generally yields higher ratios.
HEX value not recognized: Ensure you include the # prefix and use valid hexadecimal characters (0-9, A-F). Both 3-digit (#FFF) and 6-digit (#FFFFFF) formats are supported.
Palette colors look off together: Switch from complementary to analogous scheme for more subtle harmony, or adjust saturation to unify the palette.
